rubric_notes: Correct families with examples from evidence, superfamily as curated homology claim, classes/folds above superfamily too coarse, function not transferred (TAFs in TFIID), a.22.1.0 flagged as uncurated, release and limits stated. Flaw: H1/H5, H-NS, fragments and enzymes are declared 'functional or name-based associations, not homology' as a flat assertion, which goes beyond what different-fold placement supports. 'Family-level divergence' phrasing is muddled but not wrong. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct a.204.1.2/a.204.1.4, superfamily a.204.1 (sunid 101386) as lowest shared node, family/protein/species labels verified from parents and annotations. Concludes distant superfamily-level homology only, no family-level or orthology claim, rejects HisE enzyme/substrate/pathway transfer, refuses to treat MazG-like label or 'li, unl' ligand as functional evidence, and notes external evidence needed. Complete.

Correct families c.55.1.1/.3/.4 under c.55.1 (sunid 53067), fold c.55, supported by the sccs node and children responses. Superfamily rank treated as the homology call; rejects functional transfer, family-level inference, fold-only reasoning, and residue mapping. Empty name-search remark is methodological and carries no factual payload. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct superfamily/family placement and sunids for a.25.1 and its three families, correct reading of divergence within one superfamily and refusal to transfer function; rejects fold-alone homology. Omits the requested evidence standard for chemistry claims (only mentions FATCAT/sequence checks for membership questions, not biochemical/structural evidence for metal or reaction). Factual: protein node 47257 and the (apo)ferritin/dodecameric/non-hem ferritin nodes are cited but not present in this bundle (no search or protein-level calls).

Correct hierarchy (b.6.1.1/49504, b.6.1.5/74874, b.6.1.6/110107 under b.6.1/49503, fold b.6/49502) supported by the children listing; states superfamily implies common ancestry while functions are not shared and refuses copper/ET transfer. Did not retrieve the family or superfamily annotations and only names sequence/structure analysis of copper-site residues, omitting biochemical evidence as a requirement; functional statements rest on pretrained knowledge. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct sccs for the three families under d.15.1 in fold d.15, Pfam xrefs and empty superfamily comments supported by the bundle; superfamily-level ancestry, no family-level homology or function transfer; unsafe transfers include conjugation, UBX-binds-Ras, RBD-binds-p97, and fold similarity as proof of homology; p97/Ras labelled background knowledge needing experimental evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22. Correct superfamily-level probable-ancestry inference for c.23.1.4 and c.23.1.5 under c.23.1, supported by parents endpoints; rejects phosphorelay, phosphoreceiver and ODC-wing catalysis. Omits the CheY-related family c.23.1.1 identifier (admits receiver family not confirmed) and does not explicitly reject transfer of circadian regulation for the KaiA domain, only a generic 'no molecular function' statement.

Correct b.84.5 under b.84 with five sibling superfamilies, family b.84.5.1 (310616) grouping V1 and A1 entries, example domains with boundaries matching the bundle. Explicitly states that same-fold placement is architectural, that separate superfamily means SCOPe does not assert common ancestry, and that this does not prove non-relation. Release-specific caveat and PubMed rationale limit stated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct f.21/f.21.1/f.21.2/f.21.3 split with sunids, bundle-supported; correctly flags unrelated 'Fumarate reductase' hits in other folds. Central conclusion (fold ≠ homology, no merge) is right and it notes external sequence/structure comparison would be needed. Omits the explicit calibration that the superfamily split is not evidence against homology and did not retrieve the f.21.3 'possible link' curator note, so one important implication is missing. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct family sunids under c.2.1 in fold c.2 (c.2 children and c.2.1 children in bundle); PF02254 mapping supported. States shared superfamily is an evolutionary group at superfamily level only (remote homology, low sequence identity), distinct families imply no closer ancestry, and function does not transfer; notes ADH catalysis sits in other domains and that 'NAD-binding' does not mean dehydrogenase. Honestly flags that functional descriptions rely on pretrained knowledge and that c.2.1.1/c.2.1.8 comments were not retrieved. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Accurate family placement, SUNIDs, and ligand comments; caveats that the shared label is a designed-protein classification, not natural ancestry, and rejects transferring the 'Amyloidogenic' label. Did not retrieve the family node and omits the 'not a true family' annotation on SUNID 100905. Bio capped at 2 for ignoring the decisive annotation; factual 2. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct: 1.69 d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 singleton fold c.137 (sunids 110459/110460); 2.08 d1t1ja1 A:1-118 c.23.14.2 in c.23.14 (52309) with d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 (family 52310), sister families. Frames shared superfamily as classification-level inference of common origin, not function; distinguishes 1f8y label change from substantive change. Slightly overstated remark that sunids are 'not comparable across releases' (they are stable node identifiers; only parentage changed), but the comparison itself is done on lineage correctly. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete artifact lineage with sunid 343393 and sccs l.1.1.1 supported by parents and annotations endpoints; d1a14h1 H:9-111 b.1.1.1 V-set VH named as the real domain. States tag matches reflect shared synthetic sequence, not ancestry, carry no function, and do not transfer classification to a target; notes 8-residue length limit. Homology warning not cited but not required.

Strong reasoning: 1.75 whole-chain f.11.1.1 and 2.08 split to b.179.1.1/f.60.1.1, domain-as-module inference, refusal to assert independent evolution, and thorough search guidance. But its four-entry parents-only bundle supports the lineages while the stated residue boundaries and the 3tewA 96.9% figure are API-dependent claims without supporting evidence; 2.04 split release not identified.

Complete mosaic reading with correct SIDs, boundaries, and hierarchy levels; new fold d.394 for d3jb9a5; family vs superfamily distinction made; function transfer rejected. Noncentral error: claims SCOPe species labels are 'inconsistent' because the /sccs/e.8.1.8 resolver returned a S. cerevisiae species node; that is a sibling species node under the same protein, not an inconsistency with the d3jb9a3 lineage. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete: shared lineage, lengths 51/373/752, domains spanning different numbers of ~34-residue repeats, and the 're' heterogeneity flag with the 4cj9 A:259-292 representative repeat applying only to d4cj9a_. Correctly treats domain-length differences as repeat-count variation rather than separate ancestry, warns against RVD/function transfer, and notes empty Pfam/UniProt xrefs. Fully evidenced.

Reports stable 2.08 / 2.08-stable with freeze and release dates and the periodic label 2.08-2026-08-16, all matching its evidence bundle (the reported periodic label differs from the gold 2.08-2023-01-06 but is directly supported by the bundle, so not penalized). Recommends pinning release=2.08 and citing the full dated string when a periodic update is used; correctly says the periodic label is not a new numbered release. Omits the substantive periodic semantics (adds newly classified PDB entries without rewriting stable-release domains), describing it only as a 'refresh'. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly reports a.47.2.1 (STAT-like fold, t-SNARE superfamily) for d1br0a_, d1ez3a_ and d1dn1b_, cites the 'three-helical fragment; similar to one spectrin repeat' comment and 'ms' flag, the automated-matches parent (191190) vs curated node (47663), the d3c98b_ match and 1dn1 obsolescence; all bundle-supported. Makes the central inference that fragment placement is partial-coverage evidence and that 1dn1 B anchors the complete domain, with limits stated. Does not explicitly state that the full domain resolves the fragment-driven spectrin-like resemblance in favour of the STAT-like/syntaxin interpretation. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correctly explains chemical constraint, short-motif recurrence, and the evidence needed (full-domain profiles, structural alignment with topology, catalytic residues, curated placement), and notes divergence is not excluded. However, the divergence-within-superfamily point is only weakly stated ('a family within one superfamily could share descent') rather than as SCOPe's positive superfamily assertion, and it frames convergence as the default for different folds. Only c.2/c.2.1/c.3 retrieved (sunids verified); '3-layer sandwich' is a fold description misattributed to class c.

Correctly contrasts 2.04 different folds (b.23 vs b.18, only class shared) with 2.08 shared superfamily b.18.1 at distinct families, remote homology at superfamily depth, convergence noted as alternative, no function transfer. Classifications accurate.

Family-level homology retained via homology_implied_by_level; hf correctly read as weakening only the fold-equivalence claim while sequence/SSE similarity remains, domain-scoped and non-inherited; template use requires separate structural comparison; mutant/ligand states noted; recommends keeping hf as metadata, explicit handling in family splits, or exclusion from fold-level evaluation; limits stated. Identifiers, lineage, comments and homology fields all supported by the bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22. Correct lineage, boundaries, release, fr semantics (domain-level, not inherited, heterogeneity for d1o5dt2 only), protein nodes 110060 and 49267. Flag framed as completeness warning not homology rejection. Alignment: covered region only, coverage/identity statistics flagged as depressed by truncation, strand-level check deferred to external structural evidence. Representative: prefer d1uc6a1 for complete-domain sets, keep d1o5dt2 for diversity with fragment status carried as a separate attribute. Rejects cr9/function/interface transfer. All criteria met; quality not retrieved but no ranking attempted.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct central choice (new superfamily in fold), correct family and new-fold semantics, provisional-hypothesis framing present. However it describes the new superfamily as an 'unrelated-to-known-superfamilies lineage' and 'probably independently ... related', asserting nonhomology from superfamily separation; the later caveat ('not proof of non-homology') contradicts this rather than removing it. c.1 SUNID 51350 in 2.08 is supported by the bundle.

States the three families d.144.1.7, d.144.1.4, d.144.1.6 share superfamily d.144.1 (sunid 56112) in fold d.144, release 2.08; sibling families match the children response. Superfamily placement read as common origin of the catalytic core with Mg-ATP phosphotransfer, explicitly not implying same family, acceptor or regulation. Rejects transfer of regiospecificity names across APH members or to PI3K/protein kinases, and notes PI3K p85 regulation is classified separately (d.93.1.1, iSH2, SH3; correct SCOPe placements though not in the bundle). Requires activity assays with kinetics, substrate-analogue structures showing acceptor-binding residues, mutagenesis, partner/phosphorylation data, and states similarity alone is insufficient. Complete with no material error. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
